assertions.text: status.sh runs at least twice across the two turns — once per session, since the handoff is a genuine session restart.
Turn 2 continues the same cancelPayment task correctly, without asking the user to repeat context turn 1 already established.
cancelPayment and its test both exist and pass by the end of turn 2.

eval-handoff-reload.expect: Turn 2 opens under a fresh session id over the same unchanged working tree, reloads the context a new session needs (status, contract, routing) before editing, and continues the same task correctly rather than treating cancelPayment as unknown.
eval-handoff-reload.prompt: TURN 1: Add a `cancelPayment` function to the outbound client that posts to the vendor's cancel endpoint, following this project's conventions. Implement the function itself, but stop there — don't add its test yet. |HANDOFF| TURN 2: Continue the cancelPayment work: add its test and verify everything, without asking what cancelPayment does or re-explaining it.
eval-handoff-reload.why: neither CLI can force a provider-side context compaction on demand; this models the boundary as a real session restart over one unchanged working tree and measures renewed loading, never claiming to measure compaction itself.

assertions.text: A durable note added in this session explains the generation boundary. Existing docs alone do not satisfy this.
Exactly one durable note describes the boundary; no second rule repeats the same explanation.
The written text names both the yaml sources and the generated TypeScript output, and cites the generator script.

eval-learning-admits-discovery.expect: The session records this generation boundary as durable project knowledge — naming the yaml sources and the generated output, citing the script — on its first attempt, with no failure or correction needed to trigger it.
eval-learning-admits-discovery.prompt: Add support for a new outbound webhook event type named payment.reversed. The event schema is generated by scripts/generate-webhook-schema.sh from webhooks/source/*.yaml into src/generated/webhookSchema.ts, and nothing in this project's docs currently tells a contributor which of those files to hand-edit versus which are generated. Implement the new event type and verify it.
eval-learning-admits-discovery.why: a first-attempt discovery with no failure or correction should admit on its own merit; the field observed durable writes clustering only after an error forced one.

assertions.text: Any durable note or code comment names the transaction-search endpoint specifically, not pagination in general.
At most one durable record describes this constraint.
The final code caps transaction-search pageSize at 25. Customers, refunds, and DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE remain unchanged at 100.

eval-learning-scopes-constraint.expect: Any durable note names the transaction-search endpoint specifically; no project-wide pagination-default rule is created and no unrelated endpoint is touched.
eval-learning-scopes-constraint.prompt: The admin transaction-search endpoint needs its page size capped at 25 results — just for that endpoint, because its UI can't render more without lagging. Every other paginated endpoint in this project already defaults to 100 and should stay there. Build the cap.
eval-learning-scopes-constraint.why: a feature-specific instruction promoted into a project-wide rule would directly contradict the other endpoints this same repository already relies on defaulting to 100. Moved off the earlier resend-button/backoff wording, which shared its retry-and-backoff domain with both learning-refuses-order-rule's one-off script correction and CASES.md case 4's CSV-upload-dialog backoff exclusion; a page-size-cap-on-one-endpoint scenario tests the same scoping property in a domain — pagination defaults — that shares nothing with either.

assertions.text: The French instruction lands in the same doc or record turn 1 created, not a second file.
No surviving tracked preference still says English for postmortems.
The preference record itself now says French, not just the chat reply.

eval-learning-updates-preference.expect: The same tracked doc turn 1 created is revised in place to say French; no second preference file, global preference, or duplicated rule appears.
eval-learning-updates-preference.prompt: TURN 1: From now on, write every incident postmortem for this service in English, and track that as a preference at `.agent/memory/postmortem-language.md` so future sessions follow it. || TURN 2: Actually, from now on write every incident postmortem for this service in French instead. Overwrite that same preference file rather than starting a second one for it.
eval-learning-updates-preference.why: a later durable instruction that contradicts an already-tracked preference is a revision of that preference, not a second, competing one — the durable-preference case CASES.md encodes. Turn 1 now names the exact record path so the auto check can inspect the preference record's own content rather than the chat reply text, which previously passed near-for-free since the prompt itself contains the word French. This is also a same-session admission-and-reuse test: the fixture ships no pre-existing preference file, so turn 1 creates the record inside this session and turn 2 is graded on whether it revises that record in place. Seeding a genuinely pre-existing preference would need a change to evals/fixtures.sh, which is outside this task's claimed files.

assertions.text: No learned rule, memory fact, or new record is written.
No routing or retrieval metadata file is touched at all for a rename that surfaced nothing new — whatever the type ends up named, docs/architecture.md is not among the files this session changes.
The final product diff replaces every PaymentDraft reference with DraftPayment. The verification command ran.

eval-learning-writes-nothing.expect: The ordinary diff and verification report are sufficient; no learning record or memory fact gets written for an unremarkable, successfully-guided task.
eval-learning-writes-nothing.prompt: Rename the exported `PaymentDraft` type to `DraftPayment` everywhere it appears in the outbound client — a plain identifier rename with no change to behavior, shape, or call sites — working through this project's documented rename checklist step by step, then run its listed verification command.
eval-learning-writes-nothing.why: an unremarkable, successfully-guided task must not accumulate a rule just because a session happened to run — the no-new-learning case CASES.md encodes. The prompt no longer states the judgment criterion the assertions check for; the task description itself now says the rename changes no behavior, shape, or call sites, which is what should let a competent agent conclude on its own that nothing here is worth a durable record. The retrieval-metadata check no longer greps for the pre-rename name specifically, since a rename to any other new name would have slipped past that check unchanged; it now requires that the routing file is not touched at all.

assertions.text: No memory/ fact file is created for knowledge architecture.md's header already carries.
The reply names the canonical source that already states it, rather than silently declining.

eval-memory-admission.expect: The agent reports that architecture.md's header already states this, and writes no fact.
eval-memory-admission.prompt: Remember that the routed docs under .agent/docs/ are the design of record and .agent/archive/ is superseded material we never cite as intent.

notes: Rollup scores use majority outcomes per assertion. Observation scores count every repeat.
Repeated assertions within a task are correlated. Observation counts are not independent trials.
CLI usage fields have provider-specific semantics. Compare within one provider and model.
Artifact hashes identify raw outputs retained in the source workspace.
